metadata.content: Kevin Pietersen promises to challenge Brendon McCullum as England white-ball head coach eyes world No 1 ranking | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Kevin Pietersen promises to challenge Brendon McCullum as England white-ball head coach eyes world No 1 ranking England's new white-ball specialist mentor Kevin Pietersen tells Sky Sports Cricket: "There are times when Harry Brook stands at the wicket and he goes, 'This is too easy'" but adds: "I will never in my life try and take the flair and that genius out of him" Sunday 27 September 2026 23:22, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kevin Pietersen speaks to Nasser Hussain about his new role as an England white-ball mentor and how his relationship with Brendon McCullum has developed Kevin Pietersen has promised to challenge England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum in his new role as a specialist mentor to the team, saying it's precisely why he was brought in. Since retiring as a player in 2018, Pietersen has, at times, been an outspoken critic of the England setup, including when accusing the white-ball team of inadequate preparation on a tour of India last January after McCullum had just taken over. Pietersen's work with England began with a 3-0 T20 series whitewash of Sri Lanka, before the hosts then also clinched a 2-1 ODI series success over the same side on Sunday. metadata.summary: Scottie Scheffler has been widely praised for his ‘amazing’ sportsmanship after being left frustrated by American crowd behaviour during his Presidents Cup singles victory.
metadata.content: Presidents Cup: Scottie Scheffler calls out heckler behaviour and is praised for 'amazing' sportsmanship in singles win | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Presidents Cup: Scottie Scheffler calls out heckler behaviour and is praised for 'amazing' sportsmanship in singles win Nico Echavarria was disrupted by a spectator during a backswing in his Sunday singles defeat to Scottie Scheffler, who conceded a lengthy putt on the hole because of the incident; Scheffler claimed a 2&1 win as Team USA produced a 17-13 comeback victory over the International Team Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Monday 28 September 2026 00:49, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Scottie Scheffler defended Nico Echavarria after a fan in the crowd shouted during the Colombian's swing Scottie Scheffler has been widely praised for his ‘amazing’ sportsmanship after being left frustrated by American crowd behaviour during his Presidents Cup singles victory. The world No 1 faced Nico Echavarria on the final day at Medinah, where the Colombian was distracted by a spectator yelling in his backswing during his tee shot at the par-four 14th. Echavarria dropped his club and stared at the culprit as his ball finished in the right rough, while Scheffler called out the heckler. The Presidents Cup rookie then had to lay up and failed to stay on the green with his third shot. messages.text: Team USA snatch Presidents Cup thriller after epic singles fightback

metadata.summary: The United States snatched an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup victory after a remarkable final-day fightback saw claim a stunning 17-13 win over the Internationals.
metadata.content: Presidents Cup: Team USA beat International Team 17-13 after epic Sunday singles fightback to avoid shock Medinah loss | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Presidents Cup: Team USA beat International Team 17-13 after epic Sunday singles fightback to avoid shock Medinah loss Jacob Bridgeman claimed the winning point for Team USA, who dominated the Sunday singles to complete a dramatic Presidents Cup comeback at Medinah; Brandt Snedeker's side won 9.5 points during the final day to continue their dominance against the International Team Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Monday 28 September 2026 00:27, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final day of the Presidents Cup, where Team USA produced an epic singles comeback The United States snatched an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup victory after a remarkable final-day fightback saw claim a stunning 17-13 win over the Internationals. Brandt Snedeker's trailed by three points heading into the Sunday singles at Medinah, leaving Team USA requiring eight points from the final 12 matches to avoid a first defeat since 1998, but responded in spectacular fashion. Cameron Young, Justin Thomas and Scottie Scheffler all delivered points early for Team USA, only for Tom Kim and Sungjae Im to register key wins to move the Internationals within three points of a first away win in the biennial contest.
